Species Forge

Every creature here is built from your sigil drawings. One of your bodies is the frame; each of its slots can be refilled with the same slot's parts from another root, fitted into the spot the original part occupied. The forge mutates and crosses these assemblies, keeps the most coherent one for every cell of the map, and lets you breed by eye.

How one generation works

1 · Select

Pick a parent

A random elite from the map. Three times in ten it is crossed with a second elite first: each slot's donor is taken whole from one parent or the other, so tails only ever trade with tails.

2 · Mutate

Pull one lever

Re-borrow a slot from another root, resize a slot, add or cut spine links (extra links repeat the last one, shrinking), drop an optional slot, fork the spine, or move the whole creature onto a different body frame.

3 · Assemble

Fit real parts into real spots

Each donor part is scaled to the area of the part it replaces and pinned the same way: side pieces at their inner edge, tails at their root, centre pieces on the spine. Right sides use your own right-hand drawing, transformed to match the left.

4 · Judge

Keep it if it holds together

Rules stand in for "reads as one animal": nothing floating loose, no part stretched far from its drawn size, no single part stamped everywhere, no worse crowding than your original frame. It competes only inside its own cell.
